subject: Biotechnology
title: Cellular Agriculture
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cellular Agriculture.

hook.text: Grow meat from cells, not animals — cellular agriculture could feed the world without factory farms.

buildup.text: Muscle stem cells multiply in bioreactors fed with growth media — forming tissue identical to conventional meat.

discovery.text: Singapore approved Eat Just's cultured chicken in 2020 — the first country to allow lab-grown meat sales.

twist.text: Cost dropped from $330,000 per burger in 2013 to under $10 — but matching conventional meat prices remains difficult.

climax.text: Precision fermentation produces dairy proteins without cows — Perfect Day makes whey from engineered fungi.

punchline.text: Meat without the animal — cellular agriculture redefines farming.

quiz.question: How does precision fermentation produce dairy proteins?
options: It extracts proteins from plant-based milk alternatives
Engineered microorganisms like fungi produce real dairy proteins through fermentation
It uses chemical synthesis to create artificial milk proteins
